meters.label: Packets held back waiting for packet 2

frames.narration: TCP first. The sender sends numbered packets 1, 2, 3, 4 across a network that sometimes drops packets.
Packet 2 is lost in the network. Packets 1, 3 and 4 reach the receiver.
The receiver hands packet 1 to the application, but it must hold 3 and 4 back, because the application needs them in order. This waiting is head-of-line blocking.
The receiver keeps acknowledging 'got up to 1'. The sender notices packet 2 is missing and sends it again.
Packet 2 arrives, and now 2, 3 and 4 are delivered together. Nothing was lost, but they were late by a round trip or more.
UDP next. The same four datagrams are sent with no acknowledgements. Packet 2 is lost again.
The receiver uses 1, 3 and 4 the moment they arrive and shows a tiny glitch for 2. For a live call that is better than freezing while waiting for it. For a file it would be corruption.
